guide.q.customise_system: Can I change this system myself?
guide.a.customise_system: Yes. This is open-source software — the code is public, and you can change it. You can download the code from GitHub and run it yourself, or pay a web builder to do it for you. The README on GitHub explains how to put it online.
guide.q.customise_for_me: Can you change it for me?
guide.a.customise_for_me: Yes. I charge a flat rate for this work — see chobble.com/prices for current prices. I can build extra features, do branding, design listing pictures, set up hosting, or whatever you need. You own the finished code, and I can show you how to look after it or handle the updates for you. I have built web systems for over 20 years, so problems usually get solved quickly.
guide.q.hosting_and_images: Do you help with hosting and pictures?
guide.a.hosting_and_images: Yes to both. I can set your site up on your own Bunny account (or another host) and handle the technical set-up. I also design listing pictures if you need them. Get in touch and we will work out what you need.
guide.q.how_do_i_restore_from_a_backup: How do I restore from a backup?
guide.a.how_do_i_restore_from_a_backup: This one is for your web builder, because it uses a command line. Put the target database's DB_URL and DB_TOKEN in .env — the settings file next to the app's code. Then run deno task restore <backup.zip> from a copy of the app's code. The task checks the file and asks you to confirm before it deletes anything.
guide.a.are_old_backups_deleted_automati:
Yes. Only the newest backups are kept — 30 by default. When a new backup takes the count past that, the oldest is deleted. The Backups page shows how many you have and when the oldest will go.

Automatic backups made before an update count towards the limit too.
guide.q.do_backups_require_any_special_c: Do backups need anything set up first?
guide.a.do_backups_require_any_special_c: Yes. Backups are stored with your host's file storage, so the host must have it turned on. If it is not, the backup page says so. Ask the company that runs your site to set up storage for backups.
guide.q.why_does_my_site_say_it_s: Why does my site say it's in read-only mode?
guide.a.why_does_my_site_say_it_s:
Read-only mode means people can look but not book. It is switched on by the company that runs your site, not from inside your admin pages. They use it for two things: sites behind on bills, and sites being fixed.

While it is on, bookings are refused and listing and group pages cannot be changed, but everything else can still be seen. If you think your site should not be in read-only mode, contact whoever runs it for you.
guide.q.how_do_i_check_for_updates: How do I check for updates?
guide.a.how_do_i_check_for_updates: Go to /admin/update to see when your copy was built. Click Check for Updates to ask GitHub for the newest release. If a newer one exists, you see its name and number.
guide.q.what_does_the_version_number_mea: What does the version number mean?
guide.a.what_does_the_version_number_mea: Each version is named after the date and time it was built, like v2026-03-01-142500 — 1 March 2026, 2:25pm. Bigger means newer. The update page compares your copy's build time against the newest release to tell you whether an update is waiting.
guide.a.what_is_the_backup_feature: The Backups page (owners only, under Settings → Backups) saves a complete copy of everything on your site. Each backup is one .zip file that holds all your data. Backups are kept on your host's file storage, and you can download them at any time. Restoring one is done with the command shown on the page.
guide.q.how_do_i_create_a_backup: How do I make a backup?
guide.a.how_do_i_create_a_backup:
Go to Backups and click Create backup now. The site packs everything into a .zip file and stores it. Earlier backups are listed with their dates, and you can download any of them.

A very large site cannot be backed up from that page — one page visit only allows so much work. The page tells you when that happens. A web builder can still make the backup using the app's code.
guide.q.what_is_the_encryption_key_shown: What is the encryption key shown on the backup page?
guide.a.what_is_the_encryption_key_shown:
The key unlocks the personal data inside a backup. You need it only if you ever restore a backup onto a different site.

Keep the key somewhere safe. It cannot be recovered if it is lost.
guide.q.how_do_i_install_an_update: How do I install an update?
guide.a.how_do_i_install_an_update:
When an update is available and your host allows it, an Update Now button appears. Click it and the new version downloads and installs by itself. The update is recorded in the activity log.

If no button appears, your host has not allowed one-click updates. Ask the company that runs your site to update it for you.
guide.q.where_can_i_read_the_release_not: Where can I read what changed in each update?
guide.a.where_can_i_read_the_release_not: The update page links to the release notes on GitHub. They say what changed in each version, so you can decide before updating.
guide.q.customise_table_columns: How do I change which columns appear in tables?
guide.a.customise_table_columns:
This one is for people comfortable with template codes.

Open Advanced settings. Find Listing table columns or Attendee table columns. Enter a comma-separated list of tags. The list controls which columns appear and their order.

For example, use these tags to show only the name and status in the listings table:

{{name}}, {{status}}

Clear the field to go back to the default columns.
guide.q.listing_table_columns: What listing table columns are available?
guide.q.attendee_table_columns: What attendee table columns are available?
guide.q.column_format_filters: Can I change the date or money format?
guide.a.column_format_filters:
Yes. Date and price columns can use Liquid filters — extra instructions after a pipe (|):

{{created | date: "%B %d, %Y"}}
{{date | date: "%A %e %b"}}
{{price | currency}}

The date filter uses strftime codes — short codes for parts of a date. These are common ones:

  • %Y is the full year. %y is the two-digit year.
  • %B is the full month name. %b is the short month name.
  • %d is the day with a leading zero. %e is the day without a leading zero.
  • %A is the full weekday name. %a is the short weekday name.
  • %H is the hour in 24-hour time. %I is the hour in 12-hour time. %M is the minutes.

The currency filter shows a number as money. For example, 2500 becomes £25.00.

Other columns, like name and email, ignore filters. They always show their usual content.
guide.table_columns.attendee_hidden: A column is hidden when no attendee has data for it. For example, the {{email}} column is hidden when no attendee has an email address. This happens even when the column is in the template.
guide.table_reference.label: Label
guide.a.what_is_servicing:
Servicing records the times your places are used for something other than customers — jobs like a boiler service, a deep clean, or a private hire.

A service event holds a number of places on a listing for a date (so they cannot be sold) and records what the job cost. Manage them under Servicing.
guide.q.create_service_event: How do I create a service event?
guide.a.create_service_event:
Go to Servicing → New service event. Give it a name (the job), a start date and duration, then enter a Quantity against each listing it should hold — at least one. Those places are kept back for that date, so nobody else can book them.

Service events appear on the dashboard's Upcoming service events list, and are tagged Service in attendee tables.
guide.q.record_servicing_costs: How do I record what a service event cost?
guide.a.record_servicing_costs:
Open the service event. Select Record service event cost. Enter an Amount and, if you like, a Note. Choose the held Listing the cost belongs to.

Costs are listed below, and you can edit each one later. A double-click or a refresh will not record the cost twice.
guide.q.servicing_and_profit: How do service event costs affect a listing's figures?
guide.a.servicing_and_profit:
A service event cost belongs to the listing you choose. It reduces that listing's profit. Profit is income minus service event costs.

Editing a cost adds a correction instead of replacing the first amount. The total includes the first amount and all later corrections.
guide.q.custom_css: Can I add my own CSS?
guide.a.custom_css:
CSS is the code web pages use for their look — colours, fonts, and spacing. A web builder can add your own CSS:

On the Advanced Settings page, find Custom CSS, enter the styles in the CSS box, then Save Custom CSS. It loads on every page after the normal stylesheet, so it can change how things look. It is cached for up to an hour, so a change can take a little while to show everywhere.
guide.a.what_is_logistics:
Logistics is for listings your staff handle at the customer's location — deliveries, equipment hire, transport, or set-up and take-down.

Turn it on with the Logistics toggle in Settings → Logistics. Once it is on, listings gain a Needs logistics option, and you can manage your delivery vans and drivers.
guide.a.logistics_agents:
Agents are the vans, drivers, or crew you can assign to a booking's start and end — for example a delivery and a collection.

You manage them on the Logistics page, giving each a name such as "Van 1". Assign users to an agent so they can see that agent's jobs on the deliveries page. Deleting an agent clears it from any bookings it was assigned to.
guide.q.enable_logistics_on_listing: How do I turn on logistics for a listing?
guide.a.enable_logistics_on_listing:
Tick Needs logistics on the listing — the option appears only once logistics is on.

Bookings for that listing then gain start and end agent choices and times on the attendee's Logistics tab, along with a delivery address and a map pin. They also appear on the deliveries run sheet.
guide.q.charge_delivery_by_area: How do I charge delivery by area?
guide.a.charge_delivery_by_area:
Set one price for each area you deliver to. The buyer picks their area on the booking form, and that area's price is added to what they pay.

  1. Create a question such as "Which delivery area?", with one answer per area — for example "Zone 1" and "Zone 2". Assign the question to the listings you deliver.
  2. Open Modifiers and add a modifier for each area. Set the trigger to Question answer, tick the answer for that area, and give it a fixed charge with the area's price.
  3. Set Max times per order to 1 on the modifier. The charge then applies once per booking, not per ticket.

The price comes from the area the buyer picks, not from their postcode — it works like a price list, not a distance calculation. Leave Max times per order blank and the charge works like a per-person delivery fee instead. A modifier's scope makes the charge apply to only some listings.
guide.q.delivery_address_lookup: How do customers fill in their delivery address?
guide.a.delivery_address_lookup:
Customers can type their postcode and pick their address from a list, instead of typing the whole thing.

To turn this on, your host needs an account with an address lookup company. On the Advanced Settings page, find Address lookup, choose a provider, and enter the key from your account with them. The key stays on this server, and searches are remembered so your account is used less.

The search box appears when a listing collects an address, and on the admin attendee forms. The address shows on the booking's Logistics tab. The customer does not set the map pin — to pin the exact spot, search by postcode on the Logistics tab, or type the coordinates yourself.
guide.q.delivery_run_sheet: What is the deliveries run sheet?
guide.a.delivery_run_sheet:
The deliveries page lists the drop-offs and collections for the agents a user drives, grouped by day (today and tomorrow).

Each booking shows the name, listing, address (with map links), phone, and ticket token. Then each job — Drop-off or Collection, with its time and agent — and a Mark done button.

Owners and managers open it from the Calendar menu and can view any date. Agent-only users see just this page, fixed to today and tomorrow.
guide.a.what_is_image_library:
The image library holds pictures you upload once and reuse across listings, groups, and site pages. Each image has a name and optional alt text — a short description read aloud to blind visitors.

The library needs your host's file storage to be on. Until it is, the page says so.
guide.q.add_image_to_library: How do I add an image?
guide.a.add_image_to_library: Choose Add Image, give it a name, add optional alt text, and pick a JPEG, PNG or WebP file up to 32 MB. Each upload is shrunk and converted to WebP — a small, fast-loading picture type — in a full-size and a thumbnail version, so you do not need to resize pictures yourself.
guide.q.link_image_to_listing: How do I put an image on a listing?
guide.a.link_image_to_listing: Two ways. From an item's own Images tab, you can pick existing library pictures or upload a new one. Or from a picture's Edit page, you can tick the listings and groups (and, for site editors, news posts and pages) to attach it to. One picture can be linked to as many items as you like.
guide.q.delete_library_image: What happens when I delete an image?
guide.a.delete_library_image:
Pictures are shared, not owned by one item. Deleting one removes it from every listing and page that uses it. You confirm by typing the picture's name.

Pictures used by public site content (news or pages) can be changed or deleted only by site editors.
guide.a.what_are_attendee_statuses:
Statuses are labels you give a booking, such as "Confirmed". Every attendee has exactly one status, shown on their attendee page. A new site starts with a single status called Confirmed.

Manage them in Settings → Attendee Statuses, where you can add, rename, reorder, and delete them.
guide.q.status_flags: What do the Public, Paid and Reservation flags mean?
guide.a.status_flags:
Each status can carry flags — extra settings:

  • Public default — the status new public bookings start in. Only one status can hold this. Despite the name, it does not control whether anything is shown publicly.
  • Paid — the status an attendee moves to automatically once they have paid everything they owe. Only reservations advance to it.
  • Reservation — marks a pay-a-deposit-now, pay-the-rest-later status. The deposit comes from the reservation amount.

A paid status cannot also be a reservation. There is only ever one public default and one paid default.
guide.q.reservation_amount: How does the reservation deposit amount work?
guide.a.reservation_amount: The deposit amount applies to reservation statuses only. Enter 10 for a flat amount across the order, 10% for a percentage of the order total, 10x to charge per item booked, or 0 for no deposit — the attendee reserves now and pays in full later.
guide.q.assign_change_status: How do I set or change an attendee's status?
guide.a.assign_change_status:
New public bookings get the public-default status automatically. To change it, use the status dropdown on the attendee's Edit tab.

You cannot delete a status that attendees are using, the last remaining status, or the current public or paid default — move those first.
guide.q.what_is_attendees_list: What does the Attendees page show?
guide.a.what_is_attendees_list:
The Attendees page is a read-only list of every booking across all your listings, one row per attendee. Filter it by listing (or listing type), sort newest or oldest first, then move through it with Previous and Next.

To manage one listing's attendees, open that listing instead.
guide.q.export_attendees_csv: How do I export the attendee list?
guide.a.export_attendees_csv:
Use the Export CSV link on the Attendees page. A CSV is a simple spreadsheet file that opens in Excel or Google Sheets.

The export covers every booking matching the current filter, across all pages — not just the rows on screen. It includes contact details, quantity, amount paid, check-in state, and ticket links.
guide.q.where_are_attendee_actions: Where do I edit, refund, check in or delete an attendee?
guide.a.where_are_attendee_actions:
The Attendees page is for looking only. Open an individual attendee to reach their Actions tab, where you can refund, resend the confirmation, send a text, merge duplicates, or delete them. Edit their details and listings on the Edit tab.

Checking attendees in is done from a listing's own attendee list or the QR scanner.
